transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because after I eat too much, I make myself throw up so I won’t gain weight. It’s happening a lot, and honestly I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether your weight has changed significantly over the past few months?
I’m not really sure of my exact height or weight right now. I haven’t been tracking it closely, and I don’t know if it’s changed a lot over the last few months.
Do you feel that your current body weight is lower than what would be expected or healthy for your height, or has anyone—like a doctor or family member—expressed concern that you're underweight?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought of myself as underweight, and nobody’s specifically told me that I am.

When you say you eat too much before making yourself throw up, can you describe what happens during those eating episodes—do you feel like you eat a much larger amount of food than most people would in that time, and do you feel like you can't stop or control it once it starts?

Yeah. It’s usually at night, when everyone’s quiet. I’ll stand in the kitchen eating leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream—whatever’s there—and I keep going way past a normal meal. By the end it can look like half the pantry’s been picked over.
How often do these binge-eating and vomiting episodes happen, on average, and how long have you been experiencing them at this frequency?
For at least the last three months, it’s happened pretty much every week. Some weeks it’s several times, especially if I’m home more because of my back.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating (rapid consumption of large amounts of food, e.g., 'half the pantry,' with subjective loss of control) followed by self-induced vomiting to prevent weight gain, occurring at least weekly for the past three months. There is no indication of significantly low body weight or reported underweight status by patient or others, ruling out Anorexia Nervosa, binge-purge subtype. The clinical picture—recurrent binge/purge cycles with compensatory vomiting, adequate/normal weight, and preoccupation with weight control—meets criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2).
